clue.text: Where two or three are gathered together?

definitions.text: Where two or three are gathered together?

parts.words: Where two or three are gathered together?
parts.note: echoes the biblical promise about a small congregation, but read as arithmetic two plus three make five, the size of a musical group

explanation.surface: A churchgoer recalls the gospel line about a few believers meeting in prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface quotes Matthew 18:20; the question mark warns that 'two or three' should be added, giving a group of five performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of five players or singers is the ensemble formed when two and three people come together.

clue.text: One's hunted for place to excavate

definitions.meaning: the prey or target pursued in a hunt
an open pit where stone is dug out

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an animal being chased and a pit from which stone or slate is extracted.

clue.text: In firm, yours truly has earnings

parts.note: taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, the speaker

explanation.surface: A partner in a business boasts about what they take home.
explanation.definitionFit: Money coming in from work or investments is a synonym for earnings.

clue.text: Bandits ran madly from militia groups

indicators.note: running madly suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Outlaws flee in panic from armed local defenders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges BANDITS RAN; TRAINBANDS were the citizen militias of London in the 16th and 17th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained bands of citizen soldiers formed the historical part-time militia companies of English towns.

clue.text: Understood pet fell over it

indicators.note: falling over turns the word for the pet upside down, which in a down clue means reading it backwards

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a household animal tripped over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell over' looks like a stumble, but it signals reading the pet backwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied or understood without being spoken, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Order fish as s-servant comes in

indicators.note: the stammering servant enters, going inside the fish

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
a man is a servant, and the stammer doubles its first letter

explanation.surface: A diner orders fish just as a nervous, stuttering waiter arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 's-servant' imitates a stammer, a device meaning the first letter is repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: An order and a command are both instructions that must be obeyed.

clue.text: Letter in agreement

definitions.meaning: any letter of the alphabet that is not a vowel

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a non-vowel letter and also means consistent or in harmony, as in 'consonant with the facts'.

clue.text: See clever man about a horse

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree held by a learned person
RE means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone is told to consult an expert about buying a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link here, an instruction to the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A female horse is called by this name, so it is an example of a horse.

clue.text: Hypersensitive, showing ill grace, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A touchy person reacts rudely to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allergic means reacting abnormally strongly to a substance, an oversensitive immune response.

clue.text: Such a wall is so trendy to build

indicators.note: building means assembling these letters into a new structure

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashionable garden feature is described as very stylish to put up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to build' rearranges SO TRENDY; a DRY-STONE wall is built without mortar, a feature of the British countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry-stone wall is a type of wall built from stones stacked without mortar.

clue.text: Having capital in Africa, give Bill new car

parts.note: AC stands for account, which is a bill

indicators.note: new means the word car is remade in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy traveller in Africa hands over a fresh vehicle to a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is an account, AC; 'new' turns CAR into CRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Most importantly church takes scripture to be improving

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
NT is the New Testament, part of the scriptures
to rally is to recover or improve, as a patient or market does

explanation.surface: A church whose Bible teaching is said to be making it better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'to be' are links joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Centrally can mean principally or in the most important respect, as in 'centrally concerned'.

clue.text: Thinking disaster's overwhelmed mark

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so the mark ends up inside the disaster

parts.note: ruination is a disaster, utter ruin
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone muses on how a catastrophe swamped a small sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumination is deep, prolonged pondering, so it is a synonym of thinking.

clue.text: Black plague animal is a pest

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rats spread the Black Death plague

explanation.surface: The rodent associated with the Black Death is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is commonly called a pest or nuisance.

clue.text: Airline to secure piece of luggage

parts.note: an airline is an air carrier
to bag something is to secure or claim it, as in bagging a seat

explanation.surface: An airline insists on fastening down a passenger's suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic or paper carrier bag is a simple item for carrying shopping, a type of luggage.

clue.text: Support a foreigner talking of drunken revels

indicators.note: talking signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to back an alien is to support a foreigner

explanation.surface: Someone champions an immigrant while discussing wild parties.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK AN ALIEN, said quickly, sounds like the adjective from Bacchus, the god of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchanalian describes riotous drunken celebration, after the Roman festivals of Bacchus.

clue.text: Say, Bill's blushing for so mixed a career?

indicators.note: say tells us the word for bill is to be spoken and replaced by its soundalike

parts.note: a check is a restaurant bill in American usage
someone blushing turns red

explanation.surface: An embarrassed person asks whether a debt explains such an up-and-down working life.
explanation.walkthrough: CHECK, the American restaurant bill, sounds like CHEQUE; 'for so ... a career' surrounds the definition, recalling the phrase 'a chequered career'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chequered means varied or mixed in fortune, with ups and downs.

clue.text: Encourage to work melon-bed

indicators.note: working the soil turns it over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener is urged to dig a patch for growing melons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' rearranges the letters of MELON-BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To embolden someone is to give them courage, which is to encourage them.

clue.text: Make demand and invite trouble

definitions.meaning: behave so as to deserve a bad outcome

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to request something and to provoke the trouble one gets.

clue.text: Vet nursemaid, recovered from accident

indicators.note: recovered suggests covered again, so the letters are put back in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carer, having been checked over, has got better after a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' rearranges VET NURSEMAID; 'Vet' looks like a verb meaning check.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is an unlucky mishap, so it is a synonym of an accident.

clue.text: Stew, as paper's on strike

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A newspaper is in turmoil because its staff have walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a richly seasoned meat and vegetable stew.

clue.text: Breakfast food not all nice, really

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone says their morning meal is not entirely pleasant, honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and porridge are examples of a grain food eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: No longer liking a dyke-builder

parts.note: to go off something is to stop liking it

explanation.surface: Someone loses interest in a man who built an earthwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was the 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke, an earthwork along the border of England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mercian king is famous for the long earth bank named after him, so he was a dyke-builder.

clue.text: Charity event held in the mess?

definitions.text: Charity event held in the mess?

parts.words: Charity event held in the mess?
parts.note: a fund-raising occasion, but the mess suggests a muddle in which the selling takes place

explanation.surface: A fund-raiser is staged in the officers' dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: A JUMBLE SALE is a British charity sale of donated second-hand goods; jumble also means a mess, and 'mess' looks like a military canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale of assorted donated secondhand items, held to raise money for a good cause, fits a charity event.

clue.text: Thoroughly mix litre in turn

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for litre within the word for turn

parts.note: a bend is a turn in a road

explanation.surface: A cook stirs a litre of liquid in each direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend ingredients is to combine them thoroughly, so it is a synonym of mixing well.

clue.text: Elegant bird docked

indicators.note: docked, like a tail, means cut short, so the last letter of the bird goes

parts.note: a chick is a young bird

explanation.surface: A graceful bird has had its tail trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, a synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Unfancied runner-not a grey, presumably

definitions.meaning: a competitor whose chances are underestimated
jokingly, a horse with a dark coat rather than a grey one

explanation.walkthrough: A dark horse is a racing outsider; taken literally it is a horse of dark colour, so not a grey.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an underrated contender, while the literal phrase describes a dark-coated animal unlike a grey.

clue.text: Stopped working, so penniless

definitions.meaning: past tense of break down, as a machine does

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of break, as when a machine fails, and also slang for having no money.

clue.text: Saw it was thawing?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, something thawing is no longer frozen over

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT ICED, the answer describes ice melting; whole, it means saw.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed means observed or spotted, the same as saw; split in two it describes something no longer frozen.

clue.text: Hands off this clock

parts.note: sounds like a warning not to touch, but describes a timepiece that shows numbers instead of hands

explanation.surface: A warning sign tells visitors not to touch the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands off' reads as 'don't touch', but means the clock has no hands; the pun also suggests fingers, digits.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock showing the time in numerals rather than with hands is the kind described.
